clue.text: Prevented from flying, like rooks initially

definitions.meaning: trapped with no escape route, as a quarry hemmed in at an angle of walls
in chess the rooks start the game on the four extreme squares of the board

explanation.definitionFit: Trapped with no way out fits the first sense; chess rooks begin on the board's outermost squares for the second.

clue.text: Span requiring extra cunning …

parts.note: over means extra or surplus, as in left over
arch means sly or knowing, as in an arch look

explanation.surface: A bridge-building job calls for more than usual craft.
explanation.definitionFit: To span is to form a bridge or vault across something.

clue.text: Recently arrived, cheri?

parts.note: the word is a new arrangement of RICHE, and the French for new serves as the anagram instruction

explanation.surface: Someone asks a French darling whether they have just turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue drops the final i of 'cheri'; the scan shows it. Read 'nouveau' as an anagram signal applied to RICHE and you get CHERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Newly wealthy people are those who have only lately joined the moneyed class.

clue.text: Monarch involved in some golf or other game

indicators.note: being involved in something means being wrapped up inside it

parts.note: a few rounds is a measure of golf played
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the reigning queen

explanation.surface: A king or queen takes part in a few rounds of golf or some other sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British bat-and-ball game, a little like baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounders is a children's bat-and-ball sport, so it is a game distinct from golf.

clue.text: Father and son, in the end, joined artistic movement

annotationWithheld.why: Father and son, in the end, joined artistic movement: DADA + ISM fits, but no reading accounts for 'son, in the end, joined' as IS + M (or similar) without stretching
annotationWithheld.clue: Father and son, in the end, joined artistic movement

clue.text: Enticement to begin running or join in play

definitions.meaning: a lure or invitation, especially a flirtatious one
a machine or light starts working
a substitute or actor enters the field or stage

explanation.definitionFit: A lure is a come-hither noun; lights start up when switched; a substitute enters the match mid-game.

clue.text: Bird unable to take off fruit

definitions.meaning: a flightless bird of New Zealand
a fuzzy brown fruit with green flesh

explanation.definitionFit: The flightless New Zealand bird and the furry green-fleshed fruit share the name.

clue.text: Testable in crash, is it?

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters of the first word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a thing can be tested in a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a safety strap is exactly the thing tested in crash trials.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's restraining strap is the item proven in crash tests, holding occupants in a collision.

clue.text: Write off for a sort of lock

parts.note: a mortise lock is set into a recess cut in the door

explanation.surface: Someone discards a particular kind of door lock.
explanation.definitionFit: To amortise is to reduce a debt or cost gradually until it is cleared from the books.

clue.text: Lover's knot, say

indicators.note: say tells you the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: a bow is a knot tied with loops

explanation.surface: A true-love knot, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer.

clue.text: Commanding position taken just before game's decided

definitions.meaning: a place giving a good view or advantage
in tennis the point at advantage, won just before the game is won

explanation.definitionFit: A lookout spot gives a broad view; in old tennis terms 'vantage' is advantage, the point before game.

clue.text: Sport in which East repeatedly dominates arena

indicators.note: in a down clue, dominating means standing on top of the next piece

parts.note: the Orient is the East

indicators.note: repeatedly means the letter is given twice

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
a ring is an arena for boxing or the circus

explanation.surface: In some sport, an eastern side keeps on winning in the stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: Orienteering is a competitive sport of cross-country navigation with map and compass.

clue.text: Sophisticated opening 'of essay on Pope

indicators.note: on means placed after the other piece in an across clue

parts.note: Urban is the name of several popes

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A polished introduction to an essay about the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means suave and polished in manner.

clue.text: Aware it's prudent

definitions.meaning: ... of something means conscious of it

explanation.definitionFit: An old sense means conscious of something; the everyday sense means showing sound judgement.

clue.text: Inside pitcher is hidden treasure

indicators.note: inside means the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A hoard has been concealed inside a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to hold it dear.

clue.text: Part of engine arrived incomplete —— needs second handle

indicators.note: incomplete means the word is missing its last letter

parts.note: came means arrived
a haft is the handle of a knife or axe

explanation.surface: An engine part turned up unfinished and wants a handle fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A camshaft is the rotating rod in an engine that opens and closes the valves.

clue.text: Make last car trip abroad

parts.note: a spin is a short drive for pleasure
out means away from home, out and about

explanation.surface: Someone takes their final drive overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin out is to prolong something so it lasts longer.

clue.text: Found in timber over 100 tiny organisms

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a plank is a length of timber
a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: Over a hundred little creatures have been discovered in some wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are the minute drifting plants and animals of the sea.

clue.text: Extremely rare Scot's remarkable? Agreed

parts.note: unco is Scots for remarkable or strange
OK'd, okayed, means agreed to

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's exceptional find is approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely rare' looks like praise for something unusual, but steak is the subject: raw, not cooked at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked as little as possible, past rare, is raw.

clue.text: From Land's End, reported person attacking vessel

indicators.note: reported means heard said, so the word is a sound-alike

parts.note: a border is where a country's land ends

explanation.surface: News of a raider on a ship comes from the far tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of Cornwall, England, but here it is the edge of any territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarder is someone who climbs onto an enemy ship to seize it.

clue.text: Victim of street fighting sorted out crime

indicators.note: sorted means rearranged into order, so the following letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A man killed in a street brawl has his crime investigated.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercutio is the friend of Romeo killed by Tybalt in a street fight in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo's friend is stabbed during the Verona street brawl in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Superficial design for military display

definitions.meaning: a picture inked into the skin's surface
an evening show by soldiers with drums and music

explanation.definitionFit: Ink pictured on skin is one sense; a military evening parade, as at Edinburgh, is the other.

clue.text: Always having inside information about this business

indicators.note: having inside means the first word holds the others within it

parts.note: ay is an old word for ever or always
gen is British slang for information
c is the abbreviation for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone is always in possession of insider knowledge concerning a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a firm providing a service, such as a travel or advertising bureau.

clue.text: Mediator finding her rent-books out of order

indicators.note: out of order means not in the proper arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A go-between discovers a woman's rent records are a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutral go-between who negotiates impartially between disputing parties.

clue.text: Standard choice of extremes in nationalism

indicators.note: the choice word goes between the two extreme letters
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: or is the word offering a choice

explanation.surface: A typical choice of extremism within nationalist politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremes in' takes the first and last letters of nationalism, N and M; the choice word OR sits between them, reading as 'N or M'.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual standard or pattern.

clue.text: Looking very black for two of Ohio's neighbours

parts.note: IN is the postal abbreviation for Indiana, which borders Ohio
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky, which borders Ohio

explanation.surface: Something appears very dark to a pair of states next to Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky means dark as ink, deep black.

clue.text: Given up, in ironbound state

indicators.note: bound means wrapped around, so the iron encloses the state

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Oregon is a US state

explanation.surface: Relinquished while in a state bound with iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Foregone here is the past participle of forgo, meaning given up or done without.

clue.text: About to name, on oath, English outlaw

parts.note: re means about or concerning
egad is a mild oath

explanation.surface: Someone is about to name an English outlaw under oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade is a rebel or deserter who has broken with the law or their side.
